alert_details.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 9:13PM PST until November 19 at 12:15AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Marin County in northern California...

* WHEN...Until 1215 AM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 913 PM PST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Overflowing
poor drainage areas will cause minor flooding in the advisory
area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen over the last
24 hours.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
San Rafael, Novato, Mill Valley, San Anselmo, Larkspur, Corte
Madera, Tiburon, Fairfax, Sausalito, San Geronimo, Lucas
Valley-Marinwood, Kentfield, Stinson Beach, Muir Beach,
Tamalpais-Homestead, Tamalpais-Homestead Valley, Strawberry,
Black Point-Green Point, Ross and Woodacre.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alert_details.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 4:56PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at
favored break points.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

alert_details.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco County in northern California...

* WHEN...Until midnight PST tonight.

alert_details.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 4:56PM PST until November 20 at 10:00AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso Bay and San
Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at
7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45
AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
